Mahākāśyapa.question: Both these brahmin and ascetic values, as represented by the figure of Mahākaśyapa, would lead to strong opposition to the founding of the bhikṣunī order in early _____
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Both these brahmin and ascetic values, as represented by the figure of Mahākaśyapa, would lead to strong opposition to the founding of the bhikṣunī order in early Buddhism. The ascetic values Mahākāśyapa represented, however, were a reaction to less austere tendencies that appeared in early Buddhism at the time.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: His figure unites the opposites of established monasticism and forest renunciation, and "transcends any particular _____ group or set of interests"
Mahākāśyapa.fact: His figure unites the opposites of set up monasticism and forest renunciation, and "transcends any particular Buddhist group or set of interests". Buddhist studies scholar Gregory Schopen analyzes several post-canonical Buddhist texts and concludes that in both instances, a vow is taken based on psychic powers, which is then shown to be effective after the death of the person with those psychic powers.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Eventually, he came to be seen as the first teacher after the _____ and as the beginning of a lineage of teachers
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Mahākāśyapa's psychic powers are needed for his role in the texts as the one who preserves the Buddha's dispensation. Indeed, later Buddhist texts depict Mahākāśyapa as the eldest son of the Buddha, who leads both the funerals of his father and, as his heir, presides over the First Council.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: This conceptualization is found within several _____ schools, including the Theravādins and the Mahāsaṅghikas
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Indeed, later Buddhist texts depict Mahākāśyapa as the eldest son of the Buddha, who leads both the funerals of his father and, as his heir, presides over the First Council. This conceptualization is found within several Buddhist schools, including the Theravādins and the Mahāsaṅghikas.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Indeed, _____āda sees him as a sort of "Father of the Church"
Mahākāśyapa.fact: This conceptualization is found within several Buddhist schools, including the Theravādins and the Mahāsaṅghikas. Indeed, Theravāda sees him as a sort of "Father of the Church".

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Other traditional scholars have argued instead it was another Kāśyapa, who lived three centuries after the _____
Mahākāśyapa.fact: This is also reflected in the language used in inscriptions from the Sinhalese monk Mahānāman (5th–6th century CE) and in later texts used in the Sinhalese tradition, which both connect Mahānāman's lineage with that of Mahākāśyapa, and also that of the future Buddha Maitreya. Other traditional scholars have argued instead it was another Kāśyapa, who lived three centuries after the Buddha.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: They presented themselves as more orthodox than other schools, such as _____āda
Mahākāśyapa.fact: They presented themselves as more orthodox than other schools, such as Theravāda.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: He was depicted in paranirvāṇa scenes as a reassurance that _____'s dispensation would not be lost; he was depicted next to Maitreya Buddha as an anticipatory vision of the future
Mahākāśyapa.fact: He was depicted in paranirvāṇa scenes as a reassurance that Gautama Buddha's dispensation would not be lost; he was depicted next to Maitreya Buddha as an anticipatory vision of the future.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: The scene in which he paid his final respects to the Buddha became a well-known depiction in _____ art, and Strong has argued that it may have led to the cult of the Buddha's footprints
Mahākāśyapa.fact: When the differences between the early Buddhist schools grew more prominent, the Mahāsaṅghikas affiliated themselves with the figure of Mahākāśyapa, and claimed him as their founder and patron-saint. The scene in which he paid his final respects to the Buddha became a well-known depiction in Buddhist art, and Strong has argued that it may have led to the cult of the Buddha's footprints.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Fukudenkai practitioners usually use second-hand clothes to sew the rag-robes, just like in the time of the _____
Mahākāśyapa.fact: The Buddha's disciples and founders of East Asian Buddhism were often depicted in them. When fukudenkai sewing groups were set up in Japan in the early twentieth century, to introduce sewing robes for monastics as a spiritual practice, they often referred to the early Buddhist account of Mahākāśyapa receiving the rag-robes from the Buddha.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: In May _____, Sushant More, a botany researcher from Mumbai, Maharashtra discovered a new plant Lepidagathis mahakassapae endemic to the state and named it after Mahākāśyapa, following the Pāli spelli
Mahākāśyapa.fact: In May 2022, Sushant More, a botany researcher from Mumbai, Maharashtra discovered a new plant Lepidagathis mahakassapae endemic to the state and named it after Mahākāśyapa, following the Pāli spelling of his name.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: The _____ was Foster mother of Gautama Buddha and the first Buddhist nun.
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī (Sanskrit: महाप्रजापती गौतमी; Pali: Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī) or simply Prajāpatī was the foster-mother, step-mother and maternal aunt (mother's sister) of the Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: In _____ tradition, she was the first woman to seek ordination for women, which she did from Siddhartha Gautama directly, and she became the first bhikṣuṇī (Buddhist nun)
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In Buddhist tradition, she was the first woman to seek ordination for women, which she did from Siddhartha Gautama directly, and she became the first bhikṣuṇī (Buddhist nun).

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: It is recorded in the various surviving Vinaya traditions, including the _____ and Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada versions
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: It is recorded in the various surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Pali Canon and Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada versions.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: The stories of her past lives are included in the Therīgāthā, Theri-apadāna and _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: The stories of her past lives are included in the Therīgāthā, Theri-apadāna and Jataka.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She witnessed _____ place his aunt, a bhikkhuni, in a senior position, and aspired to achieve the same position after providing offerings to the Buddha and his followers for seven days
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She witnessed Padumuttara Buddha place his aunt, a bhikkhuni, in a senior position, and aspired to achieve the same position after providing offerings to the Buddha and his followers for seven days.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She was later reborn in the _____ heaven as a god
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She was later reborn in the Tavatimsa heaven as a god.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Following the rain retreat, _____ī had her followers prepare robes for the paccekabuddhas
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī then returned to the human realm as the leader of 500 female slaves. Gotamī asked the 500 female slaves to provide food offerings and convinced their husbands to build huts for the rain retreat.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near Varanasi.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī and her followers continued to perform meritorious acts throughout their lives and were reborn as _____ gods
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī and her followers continued to perform meritorious acts throughout their lives and were reborn as Tavatimsa gods.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of Gautama Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Mahāpajāpatī was both the _____'s maternal aunt and adoptive mother, raising him after her sister Maya, the Buddha's birth mother, died
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near Varanasi. Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of Gautama Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She expresses her gratitude that through the _____ (whom she addresses as "Hero"), her highest aspiration has been fulfilled and all her goals have been accomplished
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near Varanasi. Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of Gautama Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She raised _____ as if he were her own child
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She raised Siddhartha as if he were her own child.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: An eminent Therī, Mahāpajāpatī was born at _____ as the younger sister of Māyā
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: An eminent Therī, Mahāpajāpatī was born at Devdaha as the younger sister of Māyā.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Both sisters married _____, leader of the Śākya
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Both sisters married King Suddhodhana, leader of the Śākya.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the _____ (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She raised the _____ and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him. She raised the Buddha and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī went to the _____ and asked to be ordained into the Sangha three times
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him. She raised the Buddha and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the _____ kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the Koliyan kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Upon arrival, Gotamī stood crying at the entrance of the _____'s residence
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī went to the Buddha and asked to be ordained into the Sangha three times. The Buddha refused and went on to Vesāli.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Ananda, one of the principal disciples and an attendant of the _____, met her and offered to intercede with the Buddha on her behalf
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: The Buddha refused and went on to Vesāli. Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the Koliyan kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: "If that is so, Lord, then it would be good if women could be ordained as nuns," said _____, encouraged by the Buddha's reply
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Ananda, one of the principal disciples and an attendant of the Buddha, met her and offered to intercede with the Buddha on her behalf. Ananda was refused the first two times and asked the following in this third attempt: Respectfully he questioned the Buddha, "Lord, are women capable of realising the various stages of sainthood as nuns?" "They are, Ananda," said the Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Therefore, based on the Therī-apadāna (Mahāpajāpatigotamī-therīapadāna, _____ 17), Gotamī is referred to by the title "Mother of the Buddha" (Pali: Buddhamātā)
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Therefore, based on the Therī-apadāna (Mahāpajāpatigotamī-therīapadāna, Thi Ap 17), Gotamī is referred to by the title "Mother of the Buddha" (Pali: Buddhamātā).

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The _____ was Historical chronicle of Sri Lanka.
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Mahāvaṃsa (Pali: මහාවංස, romanized: Mahāvaṃsa) is the historical chronicle of Sri Lanka until the period of Mahasena of Anuradhapura.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It was written in the style of an epic poem written in the _____ language
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Mahāvaṃsa (Pali: මහාවංස, romanized: Mahāvaṃsa) is the historical chronicle of Sri Lanka until the period of Mahasena of Anuradhapura. It was written in the style of an epic poem written in the Pali language.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It was first composed by a Buddhist monk named Mahānāma at the Mahavihāraya Temple in Anuradhapura in the 5th or 6th-century.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Eugène Burnouf produced a Romanized transliteration and translation into Latin in _____, but these garnered relatively little attention

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The first printed edition and widely read English translation was published in _____ by George Turnour, a historian and officer of the Ceylon Civil Service who translated 38 chapters
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: The first printed edition and widely read English translation was published in 1837 by George Turnour, a historian and officer of the Ceylon Civil Service who translated 38 chapters.

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Louis Corneille Wijesinghe completed the remaining 62 chapters and reviewed Turnour's work, publishing in 1889.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: A German translation of the Mahavamsa was completed by Wilhelm Geiger in 1912.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: In _____, the Mahāvaṃsa was listed an item of globally important documentary heritage on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Programme's International Register

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It was written based on prior ancient compilations called the Atthakatha (sometimes Sinhalaatthakatha), which were commentaries written in Sinhala. Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: An earlier document called the Dipavamsa (4th century CE) "Chronicles of the Island" is much simpler and contains less information than the Mahavamsa and was probably compiled using the Atthakatha on the Mahavamsa as well. Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.question: These visits are not mentioned in the _____ or other early sources
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: These visits are not mentioned in the Pali Canon or other early sources.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Chronicles of Kings of _____: This material consists of genealogies and lineages of Sri Lankan kings, sometimes with stories about their succession or notable incidents in their reigns

Chronicles of Kings of Sri Lanka: This material consists of genealogies and lineages of Sri Lankan kings, sometimes with stories about their succession or notable incidents in their reigns.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: History of the _____: This section of the Mahavamsa deals with the mission sent by Emperor Ashoka to Sri Lanka, the transplantation of the bodhi tree, and the founding of the Mahavihara

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It is one of the few documents containing material relating to the Nāga and _____ peoples, indigenous inhabitants of Lanka before the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya from Singha Pura of Kalinga
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It is one of the few documents containing material relating to the Nāga and Yakkha peoples, indigenous inhabitants of Lanka before the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya from Singha Pura of Kalinga.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: As it often refers to the royal dynasties of India, the _____ is also valuable for historians who wish to date and relate contemporary royal dynasties in the Indian subcontinent

Mahāvaṃsa.fact: As it often refers to the royal dynasties of India, the Mahavamsa is also valuable for historians who wish to date and relate contemporary royal dynasties in the Indian subcontinent. Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Every chapter of the Mahavamsa ends by stating that it is written for the "serene joy of the pious". Besides being an important historical source, the Mahavamsa is the most important epic poem in the Pali language.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
